questions.question: A multinational is rolling out Agile across 12 teams on one product suite and needs portfolio budgeting, an Agile Release Train, and coordinated PI planning across all of them. Which scaling framework fits?
questions.explanation: SAFe is built for enterprise scale: Agile Release Trains, PI planning, and a portfolio layer - needs that exceed simpler multi-team options like Nexus or LeSS.

questions.question: Four Scrum teams building one product each send a delegate to a 15-minute daily coordination meeting where cross-team dependencies and impediments are resolved. Which scaling technique is this?
questions.explanation: A Scrum of Scrums is a meta-standup: ambassadors from each team synchronize work and surface cross-team blockers.

questions.question: A six-person XP team works a single story on one shared screen all day, rotating the person at the keyboard every 15 minutes while the others navigate. Which whole-team practice is this?
questions.explanation: Mob (ensemble) programming puts the whole team on one task at one workstation - unlike pair programming's two-person split.

questions.question: A Kanban team charts every step a feature takes from customer request to release, timing each stage to locate the biggest queues and sources of waste. Which Lean technique are they applying?
questions.explanation: Value Stream Mapping draws the end-to-end flow of work with per-stage timings, exposing wait states and waste for elimination.

questions.question: A support board stamps the moment a customer request arrives and the moment it ships; the elapsed total, including time spent waiting in the backlog, is tracked as the headline metric. Which metric is it?
questions.explanation: Lead time runs from request to delivery, so it includes backlog waiting; cycle time starts only when work begins.

questions.question: One Crystal coach runs a 6-person non-critical internal tool project with very light process, while a 40-person life-critical project under the same family uses heavier disciplines. What is this size/criticality-driven process adjustment called?
questions.explanation: Crystal is a family, not a single method: its colors (Clear, Orange, etc.) are selected and adjusted per team size, criticality, and priorities - methodology tailoring.

questions.question: An FDD project opens with domain experts and chief architects walking the domain and producing class diagrams plus the initial features list, before any feature team is formed. Which FDD phase are they in?
questions.explanation: FDD's first process builds the overall domain object model, which feeds the feature list; feature-level design and build happen later.

questions.question: Instead of locking an API design in month one, a Lean team keeps two viable implementations open until real performance data arrives, then commits at the last responsible moment. Which Lean principle is this?
questions.explanation: Deferring commitment delays irreversible decisions until the last responsible moment so they are made with the most information available.

questions.question: Every commit in a SaaS team that passes the automated pipeline goes straight to production - dozens of times a day, with no manual approval step at all. Which practice is this, distinct from continuous delivery?
questions.explanation: Continuous deployment auto-promotes every green build to production; continuous delivery stops at 'always deployable' and keeps a manual release gate.

questions.question: Mid-Sprint, a Scrum team plots ideal remaining work against actual remaining work each day; the actual line is flattening above the ideal, warning that scope may not finish. Which chart are they reading?
questions.explanation: A burndown tracks remaining work over Sprint time; a flat or rising actual line against the ideal trend flags schedule risk.

questions.question: Several Scrum teams must deliver one integrated product from a single Product Backlog, coordinated by a dedicated integration team. Which Scrum scaling framework applies?
questions.explanation: Nexus, created by Scrum.org, scales Scrum for three to nine teams on one product using a shared Product Backlog and a Nexus Integration Team.

questions.question: A government project has a fixed delivery date and fixed budget, but stakeholders agree low-priority features may be dropped if time runs short. Which Agile framework is built around this constraint?
questions.explanation: DSDM fixes time, cost, and quality while flexing features, using MoSCoW prioritization inside fixed timeboxes.

questions.question: A team drafts two user stories that can only ship together because each depends on the other's code. Reviewers flag the pair for violating the first letter of INVEST. What does that 'I' demand of a story?
questions.explanation: INVEST = Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable; mutually dependent stories fail the Independent criterion.

questions.question: The correct order of the three non-daily Scrum events within a Sprint, from first to last.
questions.answer: Sprint Planning, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective
questions.explanation: A Sprint opens with Sprint Planning, the increment is inspected at the Sprint Review, and the process is improved at the Sprint Retrospective.

questions.question: On an XP team, stories are written and prioritized by a real end user who sits in the team room and answers domain questions within minutes, every day. Which XP role is this person filling?
questions.explanation: XP embeds a real customer in the team to author stories, set priorities, and supply instant domain feedback - the on-site customer.

questions.question: Three days into a Sprint, the client's flagship product is discontinued and the Sprint Goal no longer makes sense. The Scrum Master wants the Sprint stopped - who alone has the authority to cancel it?
questions.explanation: Only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint, and only when the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete; neither the Scrum Master nor the team holds that power.

questions.question: A Scrum team's velocity over its last three Sprints was 30, 34, and 26 story points. Using average velocity, the number of story points it should plan for the next Sprint.
questions.explanation: Average velocity = (30 + 34 + 26) / 3 = 90 / 3 = 30 story points; yesterday's weather says plan to the observed average.

questions.question: On an Agile Release Train, all teams plan together, then deliver integrated value on a fixed multi-week cadence (typically 8-12 weeks) that closes with an Inspect & Adapt workshop. What is this SAFe timebox called?
questions.explanation: A Program Increment is SAFe's fixed cadence of iterations for an ART, bounded by PI Planning up front and Inspect & Adapt at the end.

questions.question: On a Kanban cumulative flow diagram, a band that keeps widening week over week while the bands below it stay thin indicates this.
questions.answer: A bottleneck at that workflow stage
alternatives: A growing queue / bottleneck in that stage
questions.explanation: A widening band means arrivals exceed departures in that stage, so work-in-progress accumulates there - the signature of a bottleneck.

questions.question: A startup ships a bare-bones app with a single working feature purely to test whether users want the product at all, planning to learn before building more. What is this smallest releasable version called?
questions.explanation: An MVP is the smallest release that yields validated learning about real users - not a first slice of the full feature set.
